headline: The competitor benchmark was wrong by construction: lifetime installs are legacy stock, and the live leaderboard inverted inside 8 weeks - samber/developer-relations-skills went 0 -> 3,034 w7 per listing (block 5,991 w7, momentum 75x, lifetime == 8-week sum) and now holds 78% of coreyhaines31 flow on 10% of its lifetime; our own 6 listings are only 2 live demand streams + 1 dead listing (ito-market-intelligence: 1,481 lifetime, 0 installs in 8 windows), and that dead listing is the #1 slot in the market-intelligence lane H93 told us to enter
claim: Competitor comparisons must be made on 8-week flow and momentum, not lifetime installs; listings must be decomposed into independent demand streams via co-movement (<5% rel diff => one stream); and the market-intelligence lane target from the previous cycle must be re-derived against live flow because our own rank-1 slot in it is dead.
method: read-only: 51-listing x 8-window skills.sh re-fetch (sage-cycle94-fetch.json, 04:19), scout search-rank panel (15 queries x rank 100) and headterm panel (11 terms) from 02:12, plus live ops event stream; no external writes, no publish, no repo changes

clone_check.note: no mirror inflation on our listings at these sizes

implications: Benchmark on flow+momentum; show lifetime as stock with an age index (lt/sum8) beside it. Any competitor table built on lifetime describes 2024, not now.
Decompose listing sets into independent demand streams (pairwise rel diff <5% => one stream). We are 6 listings = 2 live streams + 1 dead, not 6 channels.

Re-open H93 rule 4 (enter the market-intelligence lane): our own #1 slot in that lane is dead (0 w7 in 8 windows). Re-derive lane entry from live flow only; a lane whose leader is dead may be empty or capped - test it (T3).

Play narrow, not broad: our rank-1s are narrow single-purpose skills (2-100x margins); our losses are exactly the two broad research lanes (firecrawl, parallel-web) and the generic seo slot (#25). Do not fight firecrawl/parallel head-on.
Zero spend on renaming, consolidation, copying (H92/H93): rename correlation ~0, consolidation does not change the pool.
risks: The 51-listing panel is competitor-curated by prior cycles and may omit exactly the young entrants the disruption hypothesis is about (selection bias).
Momentum is window-dependent over 8 weeks and Q4 seasonality is uncontrolled for; F1 (samber w7 < 2000) kills the launch-run-rate reading.
Search-index installs and listing-page lifetime disagree by ~2.0-2.3x (semantics unresolved, T4); absolute lifetime numbers carry that uncertainty, ratios and momentum do not.
No revenue/usage data; installs != users. Publishing rail is sealed (0 ops_social_posts), so any positioning claim remains untestable.
tests: T1 decisive: re-fetch samber devrel pair + 2-4 other young blocks (lt/sum8 <= 1.5) for 3 more windows; inversion holds if w7 > 3500 and corey stays flat.
T2: co-movement scan for every repo with >=2 listings in the 51-listing panel; publish listing->stream map and the live-stream leaderboard.
T3 lane health: for market intelligence list every listing with lifetime >= 100 and its w7; if >=60% are dead the lane is dead, not contested.
T4 counter semantics: reconcile search-index installs vs listing-page lifetime for 10 listings; fix which surface marketplace rank uses.
T5: our live-stream share under the even-split law on a 2-stream denominator; pick the narrow slot with best expected w7.
falsifiers: F1: samber w7 < 2000 within 3 windows => launch-run-rate reading wrong; revert to dual reporting only.
F2: corey 3 listings co-move within 5% on next fetch => 5% threshold too loose, stream method collapses (our own 5 listings would merge too - more conservative for us).
F3: T4 shows both counters are the same one at different times => lifetime column is stale-by-one-window, ratios unaffected.
F4: >=3 live listings with w7 >= 50 in market intelligence => our slot is not lane leader, H93 rule 4 survives.
Kill rule: no young block out-growing a mature counterpart in any second lane => downgrade rules 1-3 to reporting-only, keep 4-6.
rules: Rank competitors by 8-week flow + momentum; report lifetime separately with age index.
New-entrant flag: lt/sum8 <= 1.5 => franchise younger than the window; treat w7 as launch run-rate, track weekly.
Co-movement discount: same-repo listings with pairwise rel diff <5% count as one demand stream (apply to us and to every competitor block).
Re-derive lane entry against live flow before spending in market intelligence.
Buy narrow slots with live flow; do not contest firecrawl/parallel head-on.
